classification.difficultyReason: Combine a similarity proof, corresponding-side calculation and an exterior angle found using trigonometry.

spec.description: Right triangle ABC with internal perpendicular DE. Alpha labels the obtuse angle BDE. Two separate dimension arrows identify DC and BC. Ordinary source-blue geometry is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AB=6 cm; BC=8 cm; EC=4 cm; D lies on BC; E lies on AC; DE is perpendicular to AC; DC=x cm; alpha=angle BDE.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated lengths or angles are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle DEC$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

answer.short: $\triangle DEC\sim\triangle ABC$ (AAA): $\angle DEC=\angle ABC=90^\circ$ and $\angle ECD=\angle BCA$.
answer.worked:
$\angle DEC=\angle ABC=90^\circ$ (given).

$\angle ECD=\angle BCA$ (the common angle at $C$, since $E$ lies on $AC$ and $D$ lies on $BC$).

The third pair of angles is therefore equal, so $\triangle DEC\sim\triangle ABC$ (AAA), with $D\leftrightarrow A$, $E\leftrightarrow B$ and $C\leftrightarrow C$.

By Pythagoras in $\triangle ABC$,
$$\begin{align*}AC&=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}\\AC&=10\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Using corresponding sides of the similar triangles,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{DC}{AC}&=\frac{EC}{BC}\\\frac{x}{10}&=\frac{4}{8}\\x&=5\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use trigonometry to calculate $\alpha$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$\alpha=126.87^\circ$.

Find the acute angle $EDC$ using trigonometry, then subtract it from $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
In right-angled $\triangle DEC$,
$$\begin{align*}\sin\angle EDC&=\frac{EC}{DC}\\\sin\angle EDC&=\frac45\\\angle EDC&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac45\right).\end{align*}$$
Since $B$, $D$ and $C$ lie on a straight line,
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac45\right)\\\alpha&=126.87^\circ\quad\text{(to two decimal places)}.\end{align*}$$
